drafts.rationale: The constitution states Foundry’s purpose as converting intent into verified running systems and keeping actual systems aligned with intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: The founding thesis says implementation artifacts are replaceable while the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, and verification obligations is the durable asset.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 1 states that no artifact is canonical merely because it exists; evidence may support or challenge intent, but existence does not create authority.
drafts.subject: Artifacts

drafts.rationale: Law 2 requires continuous reasoning about the delta between authorized intended state and actual state, and that every operation help explain, reduce, verify, or authorize that delta.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 3 forbids treating any model as canonical project memory and requires bounded compiled context; v2 applies this by making discovery output disposable and addresses Foundry-owned.
drafts.subject: Models

drafts.rationale: Law 4 requires routing to the cheapest mechanism that meets confidence, risk, and verification needs; v2 restates this as deterministic retrieval first, then cheap/strong models, then human authority.
drafts.subject: Work routing

drafts.rationale: Law 5 separates generation from verification so a creator cannot be sole authority for correctness; v2 encodes this as AI may propose but never apply a semantic state change.
drafts.subject: Generation

drafts.rationale: Law 6 treats material ambiguity as a first-class defect and requires distinguishing missing, ambiguous, and beyond-capability decisions while increasing precision only as needed.
drafts.subject: Intent

drafts.rationale: Law 7 requires distinguishing confidence, authority, and provenance; v2 preserves this by putting confidence on judgments and authority on claims.
drafts.subject: Material beliefs

drafts.rationale: Law 8 forbids research from directly mutating canonical intent and requires Research→Evidence→Reasoning→Authorization; v2 separates recorded judgments from applied transitions.
drafts.subject: Research

drafts.rationale: Law 9 requires material unknowns be resolved or explicitly controlled rather than dropped; v2 keeps conflicts in durable DISPUTED state so they cannot vanish via consolidation.
drafts.subject: Material unknowns

drafts.rationale: Law 10 requires append-only history from which current state is reconstructable; v2 uses immutable judgments, versioned issues, and event vocabulary to preserve how state became true.
drafts.subject: Meaningful changes

drafts.rationale: Law 11 requires that every meaningful artifact or behavior be explainable in terms of intent, evidence, verification, dependents, authorization, history, and intended-vs-actual divergence.
drafts.subject: Meaningful artifacts

drafts.rationale: Law 12 requires one universal lifecycle and semantic core across software, infrastructure, data, ML, agents, and future artifacts, with adapters not creating separate sources of truth.
drafts.subject: Foundry architecture

drafts.rationale: Law 13 locates global understanding in system representation rather than one model invocation; v2 requires bounded cluster inputs and Foundry-owned addresses so no single brain holds the project.
drafts.subject: Global understanding

drafts.rationale: Law 14 treats creation and operation as the same reconciliation loop at different lifecycle points and forbids splitting development and operations into unrelated control systems.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 15 requires implementations that violate the laws for convenience to change, and requires explicit evidenced amendment if a law is falsified.
drafts.subject: Foundry Constitution

drafts.rationale: The design is marked PROPOSED, awaiting architect review, not approved, not implemented, and it supersedes nothing while v1 remains frozen.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: v1 discovers the right issues then re-emits them under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1

drafts.rationale: The design’s organizing rule is that AI understands meaning while Foundry governs it: AI may propose semantic judgments but never apply them; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse transitions but never originate open-ended semantic conclusions.
drafts.subject: Meaning

drafts.rationale: Frozen 9K/9L measurements show discovery coverage identical to the baseline (31/32 critical, 55/58 overall), so the design treats discovery quality as not the problem to fix.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1 discovery

drafts.rationale: v2 treats discovery output as disposable raw evidence and interpreted governed semantic state as durable, with gaps later projected from that state.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Identity is a Foundry-owned opaque address; models only propose bindings and do not own the address, so state survives model replacement.
drafts.subject: Semantic identity

drafts.rationale: Consolidation is a state transition that merges addresses and never claims, making destruction of conflicting values structurally impossible.
drafts.subject: Consolidation

drafts.facet: role in identity and assignment timing
drafts.rationale: GapKind is removed from identity and assigned by AI only after consolidation over the consolidated issue, because kind-in-identity hid all measured same-issue different-kind duplicates.
drafts.subject: GapKind

drafts.rationale: v2 forbids treating matching subject strings, GapKind, embedding similarity, shared source events, shared ancestors, or confidence thresholds as authoritative meaning; those signals may only select comparison candidates.
drafts.subject: Semantic sameness

drafts.rationale: Option A (gap-centric) and Option B (semantic-state-first) are rejected; Option C hybrid—keep discovery framing, then governed binding/consolidation, then late gap projection—is recommended.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2 architecture

drafts.rationale: An address is identified by address_id; subject, facet, and scope are human-readable descriptors never compared for equality to decide identity.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: Claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged; conflicting values at one address become separate claims.
drafts.subject: SemanticClaim

drafts.rationale: An issue is the consolidated unresolved thing at exactly one address, and one address holds at most one live issue so the emitted set can be minimal.
drafts.subject: SemanticIssue

drafts.rationale: EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation and merges addresses not claims; CONFLICTS_WITH never merges, and NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, OVERLAPS, and DISTINCT also do not merge.
drafts.subject: Semantic relations

drafts.rationale: Retrieval decides what deserves comparison and is explicitly approximate and non-authoritative, except already-bound addresses whose meaning was previously admitted via an AI binding.
drafts.subject: Candidate retrieval

drafts.rationale: A conflict is first-class state: admitted CONFLICTS_WITH sets DISPUTED, no consolidation may clear it, and no transition may reduce distinct claim values at an address.
drafts.subject: Semantic conflicts

drafts.rationale: BUNDLES never merges; AI must propose split seams, and Foundry enforces that unit evidence unions equal the parent edge set without using sentence boundaries as seams.
drafts.subject: Bundled candidates

drafts.rationale: Materiality is an AI judgment over compiled existing decisions, authority, and supersession, not isolated prose; Foundry only compiles inputs and projects a gap when unresolved and material.
drafts.subject: Issue materiality

drafts.rationale: Grounding is an AI entailment verdict per cited event (SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED); a valid source ID is never proof of substantive grounding.
drafts.subject: Semantic grounding

drafts.rationale: Gap is a deterministic projection from persistent issues, not the durable object; the durable object is the issue at an address, and DISPUTED issues cannot be relation-suppressed from state.
drafts.subject: Gap

drafts.rationale: Wrong interpretations are corrected by append-plus-supersede, never destructive mutation; every merge retains contributing candidates and evidence so it is reversible.
drafts.subject: Semantic interpretation

drafts.rationale: Slice 1 keeps frozen v1 discovery, then retrieval, bounded cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, late classification, and gap projection in-memory for a single run, without cross-run persistence or supersession machinery.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The testable claim is that a governed semantic pipeline can preserve frontier-level critical recall while improving precision and lowering redundancy and unsupported rate versus one-shot analysis; the lifecycle-persistence claim is explicitly not yet asserted.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: An open architecture question blocks validation framing: whether v2 must pass a cleaner single-pass experiment or the lifecycle experiment, depending on whether per-cycle discovery remains differentiating.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2 validation
